title: HarnessConfig
description: Per-project configuration for Claude Code Harness. Lives at <projectRoot>/harness.config.json.

projectName.description: Human-readable project name shown in messages.

protectedDirectories.description: Directory names that R10 refuses to delete via rm/rmdir/unlink. Empty array disables R10.

protectedEnvVarNames.description: Environment-variable names R11 blocks in Bash commands. Empty array disables R11.

protectedFileSuffixes.description: File suffixes whose direct read (cat/head/tail/less/more/open/echo) R13 blocks.

sync.description: Tunables for the codex-sync agent. Mitigates mid-response truncation when Claude Code's TASK_MAX_OUTPUT_LENGTH (default 32000, documented max 160000) is exceeded by a Codex review output. `harness doctor` uses these thresholds to warn the user when the effective env var is below the runtime default without hardcoding the limit. See agents/codex-sync.md for the user-facing remediation path.

recommendedTaskMaxOutputLength.description: Value `harness doctor` prints as the recommended setting for TASK_MAX_OUTPUT_LENGTH. Claude Code silently clamps higher values so advertising one would be misleading.

warnTaskMaxOutputLengthBelow.description: Threshold below which `harness doctor` flags the current effective TASK_MAX_OUTPUT_LENGTH as WARN. Default mirrors Claude Code's runtime default so the doctor warns whenever the env var is unset.

checkTaskMaxOutputLength.description: When true, `harness doctor` reports the effective TASK_MAX_OUTPUT_LENGTH alongside codex plugin detection. Set false to silence the report entirely.

work.description: Settings consumed by /harness-work, /tdd-implement, /parallel-worktree, and core hooks (stop / subagent-stop / pre-compact / task-lifecycle).

plansFile.description: Relative path to the project's task / plan file. Consumed by pre-compact and task-lifecycle hooks to read assignment tables before compaction.

taskTrackerMode.description: Task source consumed by /harness-work and related dispatchers. `plans` (default) reads the legacy flat `Plans.md` markdown file. `handoff` opts into the 4-layer handoff structure (roadmap / backlog / current / decisions). When set to `handoff`, `handoffPaths` MUST be populated with all four file paths; missing or malformed entries trigger a stderr warning and silent fall-back to `plans` mode so skills never see an undefined dispatch source.

handoffPaths.description: 4-layer handoff document paths required when `taskTrackerMode === "handoff"`. All four entries are project-relative (anchored at projectRoot); absolute paths and `..` segments are rejected at load time. Wholesale-replace semantics — the user-supplied object is used verbatim (no merge with defaults) because partial overrides would yield silently incomplete configs. The field is preserved for forward-compat when `taskTrackerMode === "plans"` (an author can flip the mode later without re-typing the paths).

roadmap.description: Phase / Week / Task definition file with YAML frontmatter (source-of-truth for AC, depends_on, estimated).

backlog.description: Priority-ordered dispatchable view consumed by /harness-work. Contains heading-driven entries plus optional YAML metadata blocks.

current.description: Bird's-eye index file consumed by /session-handoff check (Latest state / Top priority / Quick-start).

assignmentSectionMarkers.description: Section header keywords used to locate the assignment table inside the plans file. Supports ja/en projects. First-match wins.

handoffFiles.description: Project-specific session-handoff file paths that /harness-work and /parallel-worktree update when closing a session. Existence-optional (if a listed path is missing, the hook skips it silently).

changeLogFile.description: Optional relative path to a project-local change log consumed by /harness-plan sync. If unset, sync skips change-log scanning.

testCommand.description: Canonical test command surfaced to /harness-work and /harness-release as their test step when set. Consumed by the orchestrator commands, **not by the Stop / SubagentStop hooks** (those hooks still rely on per-stack autodetection via detectAvailableChecks()). Example: 'pytest -q' for a Python project, 'npm test' for a Node project.

qualityGates.description: Per-project override of harness quality gates. Consumed by stop.ts to emit reminders.

enforceHarnessWorkEssence.description: Cross-cutting workflow reminder summarising the docs/harness-work-essence.md contract. Default-off; set true to add the bird's-eye essence reminder to the per-phase quality gates.

disciplineLedgerPath.description: Project-relative path to a markdown file where /harness-merge-train and the ledger CLI wrapper append discipline-violation entries. Absolute paths and '..' segments are rejected. When unset the ledger writer is a no-op.

pipelineCheckPath.description: Optional project-relative path to a pipeline-verification runbook (e.g. `.claude/skills/<project>-local-rules/references/pipeline-check.md`). Consumed by /harness-work to surface a project-specific addendum on top of the stack-neutral built-in checks. Absolute paths, `..` segments, empty strings, and control-character payloads are rejected at load time and fall back to undefined with a stderr warning.

parallelMode.description: Project-side default for /harness-work's parallel implementation engine. Precedence (highest first): `--parallel-mode=v1|v2` CLI flag → opt-in auto rules when `allowAutoModelB` is true → this config default → `v1` fallback. `v1` (default, back-compat) delegates Parallel/Breezing modes to /parallel-worktree (Model A). `v2` delegates to /parallel-worktree-v2 (Model B, per-worktree independent claude processes). Resolver: `core/src/work/parallel-mode-resolver.ts`.

allowAutoModelB.description: Opt-in gate for /harness-work v6 auto Model B downgrade rules. Sits at precedence step 2 of the resolver chain (`--parallel-mode=v1|v2` CLI flag → these auto rules → `parallelMode` config default → `v1` fallback). When true, the resolver picks `v2` automatically when `n_tasks >= 2 && recent_subagent_failures >= 2` (failure-history rule) OR `n_tasks >= 3` (task-count rule). Default false preserves v5 behaviour exactly — auto rules are silent until explicit opt-in. Resolver: `core/src/work/parallel-mode-resolver.ts`.

allOf.description: When taskTrackerMode is 'handoff', require handoffPaths so the dispatcher cannot fall through to undefined behavior.

security.description: Settings consumed by security-auditor agent. Lets projects supply their own stack-specific security checklist without modifying plugin core.

projectChecklistPath.description: Relative path to a project-local security checklist (e.g. `./AGENTS.md`, `./docs/security.md`, or a SKILL.md reference). security-auditor agent loads this file as addendum when present; otherwise runs the stack-neutral generic checklist only.

enabledChecks.description: Enabled security check categories. `project-specific` is effective only when `projectChecklistPath` is set.

review.description: Settings consumed by /harness-review and the generic harness:reviewer agent. Mirrors security.projectChecklistPath but is reviewer-side; lets projects supply their own review runbook without modifying plugin core.

projectChecklistPath.description: Optional project-relative path to a review runbook / addendum (e.g. `.claude/skills/<project>-local-rules/references/review-runbook.md`). /harness-review and harness:reviewer load this file as addendum when present; otherwise run the stack-neutral generic runbook only. Absolute paths, `..` segments, empty strings, and control-character payloads are rejected at load time and fall back to undefined with a stderr warning.

pseudoCoderabbitProfile.description: CodeRabbit 公式 profile は chill/assertive のみ。strict は harness-local 拡張。

plan.description: CodeRabbit subscription tier driving bucket allocation. `pro` (default) keeps the legacy single-bucket prediction (5 PR reviews / hour). `oss` enables the dual PR + CLI buckets the OSS plan exposes. `free` documents that the project has no automated review.

prReviewBucketSize.description: PR review bucket size per `proBucketWindowMinutes` window. On Pro (default) this is 5. On OSS, CodeRabbit publishes a lower per-hour PR quota — set this to `2` explicitly when `plan` is flipped to `oss` (no automatic fallback is applied; mergeConfig keeps the user value verbatim). New code paths read this field; `proBucketSize` is preserved for backwards compatibility.

cliReviewBucketSize.description: CLI review bucket size per `proBucketWindowMinutes` window. Default `0` means the CLI path is unavailable for this plan (Pro / Free). OSS exposes `2/h` independent of the PR bucket — set this to `2` explicitly when `plan` is flipped to `oss` (no automatic fallback).

tooling.description: Stack-detection knobs consumed by core hooks (e.g. subagent-stop.ts's detectAvailableChecks). Stack-neutral defaults are deliberately generic; project-specific layouts (like `backend/`) are opted in via override.

pythonCandidateDirs.description: Directory names checked for Python source when picking lint/typecheck targets. A directory is included only if it exists at `projectRoot`. Each entry must match `/^[a-zA-Z0-9_.-]+$/` (alphanumerics plus `_` / `-` / `.` — no path separators, whitespace, or shell metacharacters); rejected entries are warned about and dropped. Default omits `backend/` to avoid forcing a layout assumption; projects with a `backend/` tree add it explicitly. Edge cases: an **empty array** `[]` or any non-string / empty-string entry is treated as a malformed override and falls back to the default (this is safe — it never produces an unexpected empty lint target). To intentionally skip Python linting entirely, list a directory name that does **not exist** in the repo (e.g. `[".no-python-lint"]`); the existence check filters it out and ruff / mypy are skipped. Listing an existing empty directory does **not** skip linting — the tool will still run against it and find no Python files.

release.description: Settings consumed by /harness-release, /branch-merge, and /new-feature-branch. Projects that follow a two-branch (main only) or three-branch (main + dev + feature/*) flow surface their choice here so the plugin can stay stack/branch-neutral.

strategy.description: Branch-merge strategy. `three-branch` = feature/* → dev → main (default, matches /branch-merge spec). `two-branch` = feature/* → main directly (simpler trunk-style repos).

integrationBranch.description: Intermediate branch name in the `three-branch` strategy. Ignored when `strategy` = `two-branch`.

productionBranch.description: Final / production branch name. Used by /branch-merge and /harness-release for tag placement.

testCommand.description: Command run before each merge step. When unset, /harness-release falls back to `work.testCommand` and finally to per-stack autodetection.

userPromptSubmit.description: Settings consumed by the UserPromptSubmit hook. Acts as the harness Global plugin → Local project rules bridge: each user prompt is augmented with project-local context files (e.g. `.claude/rules/coding-style.md`) so Claude inherits invariants the project owner cares about, without forcing the user to re-paste them. Empty `contextFiles` (default) makes the hook a no-op.

contextFiles.description: Project-local context file paths (relative to projectRoot) appended to each user prompt as `hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext`. Missing files are skipped silently. Path-traversal entries (containing `..`) and absolute paths are rejected and skipped.

maxTotalBytes.description: Total byte cap across all contextFiles. Excess content is truncated with an inline marker so Claude can detect the boundary.

fenceContext.description: When true, the injected context block is wrapped in fence markers with a per-request 12-hex-char nonce (`===== HARNESS PROJECT-LOCAL CONTEXT <nonce> =====` / `===== END HARNESS CONTEXT <nonce> =====`) so the user / reader can attribute the content to the harness. The nonce defeats context-boundary spoofing attempts by literal fence markers embedded in rule file content.

postToolUseFailure.description: Settings consumed by the PostToolUseFailure hook. Fires when a tool execution fails (exception / non-zero exit / interrupt). Injects failure diagnostics and optional corrective hints into `hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext` so Claude can decide next-turn recovery without extra prompting.

enabled.description: If false, the hook returns approve with no additionalContext (silent skip). Default true.

maxErrorLength.description: Maximum length of the raw error string before truncation. Excess is cut with an inline marker.

correctiveHints.description: When true, append harness built-in corrective hints for well-known error patterns (permission denied / no such file / command not found / signal abort / timeout / network unreachable). Set false to inject raw error only.

subagentStart.description: Settings consumed by the SubagentStart hook. Fires when the Task tool spawns a subagent (before the subagent runs). Per Anthropic official spec (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks) SubagentStart is informational only — `decision: "block"` is NOT supported; blocking belongs to PreToolUse on the Task call. The handler emits `hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext` which is injected into the subagent's initial context, bridging global plugin defaults to per-type guidance (e.g. `harness:worker` → TDD reminder).

enabled.description: If false, the hook returns approve with no additionalContext (silent skip). Default true.

maxIdentifierLength.description: Maximum character length for `agent_type` / `agent_id` rendering. Overlong identifiers are truncated with an inline marker containing the per-request nonce so attackers cannot pre-compute a spoofed variant.

fenceContext.description: When true, wrap the diagnostic in fence markers with a per-request 12-hex-char nonce (`===== HARNESS SubagentStart <nonce> =====` / `===== END HARNESS SubagentStart <nonce> =====`) so the subagent can attribute the content to the harness. The nonce defeats context-boundary spoofing attempts by literal fence markers embedded in `agentTypeNotes` values (attackers cannot predict the per-request value, collision probability 2^-48).

agentTypeNotes.description: Per-agent-type guidance notes. Key matches `agent_type` verbatim (undefined input coalesces to `"unknown"` — use the key `"unknown"` to target it). When a note is present for the spawning agent type, the sanitized value is appended to `additionalContext`. Non-string values and empty keys are silently dropped (shape-defensive).

maxTotalBytes.description: Total byte cap for the emitted `additionalContext`. Excess is truncated with an inline marker so the subagent can detect the boundary.

imageGeneration.description: Image-generation skill registry consumed by `run-ai-images` (engine) and `ai-image-edit` (wrap). Sets the default backend, model, reasoning effort, aspect ratio, count, and ref-image allowlist for the OpenAI image_gen tool driven through the Codex CLI. Defaults match the v0 `codex-image-gen` backend (gpt-5.4 / medium / 1:1 / 4 images). Per-agent overrides flow through `models.agents.image-gen` / `models.agents.image-edit`; the resolver (`resolveImageModel` in `src/models/resolver.ts`) emits precedence: agent-override > image-default > harness-default. Schema is strict (additionalProperties: false) — adding a new knob requires updating both the schema and the resolver to consume it.

defaultBackend.description: Backend script name resolved against `${SKILL_DIR}/scripts/backends/<name>.sh`. v0 ships `codex-image-gen` (Codex CLI + OpenAI image_gen tool); future backends (Anthropic / OpenAI SDK direct) plug in by adding sibling scripts and updating this value. Override via `RUN_AI_IMAGES_DEFAULT_BACKEND` env var at invocation time.

defaultModel.description: Codex model slug used by the default backend. Intentionally diverges from the text-side `HARNESS_DEFAULT_MODEL = gpt-5.5` because the OpenAI image_gen tool is currently only available on `gpt-5.4` (Codex CLI tool surface). May reference an alias declared in `models.codex.aliases`. Override at runtime via `RUN_AI_IMAGES_CODEX_MODEL` env var.

defaultReasoning.description: `codex exec --effort` value injected when the backend is invoked. Restricted to {medium, high} — image_gen tool does not benefit from minimal/low/xhigh in practice and a narrower surface keeps the validation predictable. Out-of-enum values fall back to `medium` with a stderr warning.

defaultAspect.description: Default aspect ratio when callers do not pass `--aspect`. Backend honours these as native output (no resize) so quality is preserved. The 5 ratios cover the most common UX targets (square / horizontal photo / vertical photo / landscape video / portrait video). Out-of-enum values fall back to `1:1` with a stderr warning.

defaultCount.description: Default number of images generated in parallel when callers do not pass `-n`. 16 upper bound mirrors `work.maxParallel` / `worktree.maxParallel` to keep fan-out reasoning consistent across the surface; 1 lower bound prevents accidental zero-fan-outs.

refImageAllowlistPrefixes.description: Absolute path prefixes that ref-image arguments are intended to start with. Empty array (default) = unrestricted (local-user trust boundary). Non-empty array = the harness loader sanitises the list so each entry is a non-empty absolute path free of `..` segments / control characters. Validation runs at config load time; runtime enforcement at invocation is the consumer's responsibility — skill scripts that drive the backend (such as `run-ai-images` / `ai-image-edit`) should reject `--ref-image` paths that fall outside the listed prefixes before the backend runs. Wholesale-replace semantics — overriding the array drops the empty default entirely.

models.description: Model registry consumed by every harness-dispatched Codex invocation (`codex-sync` / `codex-team` / `coderabbit-mimic` / `tdd-implement`). When this section is omitted the resolver reports `source: "harness-default"` (compile-time fallback `HARNESS_DEFAULT_MODEL` in `src/models/resolver.ts`). Use `codex.default` for a single harness-wide pin, `codex.aliases` to name logical tiers, and `agents.*.model` / `agents.*.reasoningEffort` to override per Codex agent. Schema-level `default` annotations are deliberately omitted so schema-aware editors do not pre-populate these values — absence is semantically meaningful (distinguishes shipped behaviour from explicit pin).

codex.description: Harness-level Codex model settings applied when no per-agent override exists.

default.description: Codex model slug served by the Codex CLI (e.g. a `gpt-X.Y` or `gpt-X.Y-codex` variant). May reference a logical name declared in `aliases`. Resolved by `harness model resolve <agent>` and injected as `codex exec --model <slug>` at agent invocation time. When omitted the resolver falls back to `HARNESS_DEFAULT_MODEL`.

reasoningEffort.description: `codex exec --effort` value. The 5 levels match the Codex config-reference documentation. Per-agent overrides under `agents.*.reasoningEffort` take precedence. When omitted the resolver falls back to `HARNESS_DEFAULT_REASONING_EFFORT`.

aliases.description: Logical-name → concrete-model-slug map so projects can say `default: "strong"` / `default: "fast"` instead of hardcoding the slug everywhere. Alias lookup runs once at resolve-time; circular or missing aliases return the literal name (surfaced by `harness model check --strict` as `unknown-slug`).

agents.description: Per-agent model overrides. Keys are agent names as understood by the resolver (`codex-sync`, `codex-team`, `coderabbit-mimic`; the resolver strips the `harness:` prefix and `.md` suffix before lookup). An entry without `model` simply inherits `codex.default`.

model.description: Overrides `codex.default` for this agent. Can reference an alias.

environmentManifest.description: Per-project infra version / known infrastructure limitation manifest. Coordinator (parallel-worktree / harness-work / tdd-implement) injects this into worker prompts so subagents can detect infra-driven failure (e.g. local DB version differs from CI) without exploring forbidden workarounds. Free-form object; common sub-keys: `postgres` / `node` / `ci_environment` / `forbidden_workarounds`. Materialization algorithm (JSON → markdown bullets) and worker prompt injection are documented in `commands/parallel-worktree.md` 'Environment Manifest injection'. When omitted, coordinator emits an empty manifest section meaning 'no declared infra constraints, INFRA_BLOCKED is still a valid retreat path'.

clarify.description: Configuration for the `/harness:clarify` skill (depth-first interview). Controls how each AskUserQuestion option `description` is composed per absolute rule 7 (audience-aware double-expression + concrete example). All keys optional (`required: []` is explicit so future maintainers don't need to infer it); defaults equivalent to `{ audienceLevel: "both", includeConcreteExamples: true, exampleCount: 1 }`. See `commands/clarify.md` § '絶対原則' rule 7 for the rendering contract.

audienceLevel.description: Target reader for the question `description` text. `both` (default) renders all three lines (ベテラン / 初学者 / 例). `beginner` and `senior` still render all three but emphasise their respective layer; the other layer is kept as a 1-line skim aid rather than removed (operator should never lose information just by changing this knob).

includeConcreteExamples.description: When true (default), each `description` includes at least one concrete `例: ...` line tied to the actual codebase / domain. Set to false only when running rapid-fire follow-up questions where examples become repetitive (the `例:` line can be omitted but the dual-audience lines stay).

exampleCount.description: Number of `例: ...` lines per option `description`. 1 (default) is sufficient for most binary or 2-3 way choices. 2-3 is appropriate when the trade-off requires comparing concrete scenarios side-by-side (e.g., parent-child cascade vs restrict on multiple table pairs). Upper bound 3 reflects clarity degradation in option `description` text when >3 examples crowd the 1-3 sentence envelope of `AskUserQuestion`; if more concrete cases are needed, prefer splitting into multiple sequential clarify questions over packing into one option `description`.

repoKind.description: Whether this repository consumes the harness or is the harness itself. Gates self-referential checks.

contextBudget.description: Context budget audit: size / dead-link / committed entry-point gates. Opt-in — every integration point is a no-op while `enabled` is false.

budgetBytes.description: Byte ceiling summed across markdown under `autoLoadDirs`.

autoLoadDirs.description: Directories whose `.md` files load into every session. Walked recursively with no pruning — a repository root would sum vendored and VCS directories too — so keep entries narrow. An empty array skips the size gate.

onDemandDirs.description: Directories loaded on demand. Excess auto-load content is redirected here, and the dead-link gate scans them.

entryPointFiles.description: Committed entry points that must reference at least one `onDemandDirs` path.

indexFile.description: Optional index file whose absence demotes the entry-point gate to WARN. Empty disables the check.
